title: A propeller-shaped μ4-carbonate hexanuclear dysprosium complex with a high energetic barrier to magnetisation relaxation

material_class.structural_family: propeller-shaped μ4-carbonate Dy6 of two Dy3 triangles

synthesis.procedure: The ligand H2bsc was prepared by mixing an ethanol (20 mL) solution of carbohydrazine (0.005 mol, 0.450 g) with an ethanol (20 mL) solution of salicylaldehyde (0.010 mol, 1.1 mL), stirring and refluxing overnight, then filtering the white powder, washing with dichloromethane and drying in vacuo (yield 98%). Complex 1: a MeOH (15 mL) solution of DyCl3·6H2O (0.5 mmol, 0.189 g) was mixed with a MeOH (15 mL) solution of H2bsc (0.25 mmol, 0.075 g) and KOH (4 mmol, 0.056 g) to give a homogeneous yellow solution. After stirring for 10 min the solution was filtered and crystallized by slow evaporation. After one week, light yellow crystals were collected by filtration, washed with ether and dried in vacuo. The main text states that carbonate is captured from atmospheric CO2 under basic conditions; an air-free reaction gave no crystals, while addition of K2CO3 under air-free conditions gave small crystals whose IR matched 1.
synthesis.time: ligand refluxed overnight; complex stirred 10 min then crystallized for one week
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution mixing followed by slow evaporation; carbonate incorporated from air under basic conditions
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered after 10 min; slow evaporation for one week; light yellow crystals filtered, washed with ether and dried in vacuo

properties.summary: Discrete Dy6 single-molecule magnet with a toroidal arrangement of the Dy(III) anisotropy axes. χT is close to the six-ion free-ion value at room temperature and falls on cooling, consistent with anisotropy/depopulation plus weak antiferromagnetic interactions at low temperature. Zero-field ac susceptibility shows a single slow-relaxation process with Ueff/kB = 101.9(9) K; an applied dc field has little effect at 2 K, indicating inefficient zero-field quantum tunnelling.
